terms.gloss: to be oneself, be in one’s senses
evidence: Ter. Heaut. 5.1.48: prae īrācundiā, Menedēme, nōn sum apud mē (Lewis & Short s.v. apud)
terms.comment: Literally “to be at home with oneself”: Lewis & Short, “to be in one’s senses”, only in conversational language and most frequent in Terence; usually negative, nōn sum apud mē, I am beside myself.
Compos, “master of”, with the genitive: so compos suī, self-controlled (Traupman 157).

sources: Lewis & Short: apud
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency.
